$comment: issue #3811 — the SINGLE data-driven source of truth for sparq's banned-terminology
gate (scripts/check-terminology.py). Adding a future banned term is ONE object in `terms`,
not a code change.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the terminology gate previously hard-coded its banned list in Python AND
scanned only `*.md`. A banned term therefore reached PR #3451 as a `pub` Rust type name and as
an rdfs:comment inside a PUBLISHED vocabulary (.ttl) with a green `ci-summary / gate` — neither
file extension was in the gate's surface. Terms now declare their OWN surface, so a term that
must not appear in code/vocabulary is checked in code/vocabulary.
SCHEMA (validated by scripts/tests/test_banned_terminology.py):
allowMarker  — the inline per-line opt-out token; the text after `<marker>:` is the required
human justification. This is the ONLY narrow escape, and it is reviewed in the
diff like any other line.
surfaces     — named file surfaces. `include` = git-ls-files globs; `exclude` = git pathspec
exclusions. A term references one by name.
terms[]      — id, label (the operator-facing 'say this instead' message), patterns (Python
`re` sources), ignoreCase, surface, allowPatterns (regexes whose match on a
line exempts it — proper nouns, citations, third-party doc names, URLs),
exemptPaths (EXPLICIT paths/globs, each with a `why`).
EXEMPTION DISCIPLINE: `exemptPaths` entries are enumerated and individually justified. Adding a
broad path exclusion to make a violation pass defeats the gate; fix the wording, or mark the one
line with the inline marker + a reason.

docs-markdown.why: The user-facing + governance markdown surface the other docs-quality HARD gates use (root *.md + skills/ + docs/ + crates/ + book/).

authored-source-and-docs.why: Everything a human AUTHORS that ships or is published: Rust/TS/Python/shell source, RDF vocabularies (.ttl/.jsonld/.yaml.ld), Noir circuits, Typst papers + specs, manifests, CI workflows, and all markdown INCLUDING research/. This is the surface a term banned from PUBLIC API + PUBLISHED VOCABULARY must be checked over — the #3811 gap was exactly that `.rs` and `.ttl` were unreachable.

excludeWhy..beads/**: A machine-synced MIRROR of the GitHub issue tracker, not authored product text. Issue titles legitimately name a banned term in order to ban it (e.g. issue #3811 itself), and the mirror is rewritten by tooling, so a hit there is neither authored nor fixable in the diff that trips it.
excludeWhy.vendor/**, target/**, node_modules/**, l: Not authored by this repo — vendored upstream sources, build output, and resolver-generated lockfiles.

exemptPaths.why: The terminology GUIDE itself — it must print each banned spelling in its 'say this, not that' table in order to ban it. Same class as the gate's own definition files.

terms.label: the banned trust-container term (say: "trust requirements" for the TR document, or a request/contract-carrier name such as ContractRequest for the (query, requirements, nonce) triple)
terms.why: Maintainer directive (2026-07-06, MEMORY feedback-no-trust-envelope-term): the term is banned in trust-program artifacts. It reached PR #3451 as `pub struct` + a PUBLISHED rdfs:comment before any mechanical check existed (issue #3811). Note the approved phrasing 'trust requirements' names the TR graph, which is ALREADY a distinct type — so the container needs a different non-banned name, not a blind substitution.

exemptPaths.why: This file DEFINES the term; the `why`/`label` prose necessarily discusses it.
The gate implementation documents, in prose, which term it bans and why.
The both-direction self-test asserts on literal should-FAIL strings containing the term.
Deliberate violation fixtures — the mutation evidence that the gate is non-vacuous. They exist to be caught when scanned EXPLICITLY by the test; they must not red the repo-wide scan.

allowPatterns.$comment: Line-level exemptions, keyed by term id. A line matching any regex here is a legitimate proper-noun / citation / third-party-doc-name / URL usage and passes.
